claim_short: Agentic tools went from writing 20% to 80% of 'your' code over December

Asked how founders should build, Brockman answers 'I would say to lean in' and then says agentic tools went from 'writing 20% of YOUR code to writing 80% of YOUR code' over the course of December. The subject is the customer's code, not OpenAI's. No figure for OpenAI's internal code appears anywhere in the 28-minute talk. Actual wording is hedged and v0's paraphrase removed the hedges: 'I think that we went from these agentic coding tools being like, you know, they're like writing 20%...'. Timestamp 07:32-07:41. 'Over the course of December' CONFIRMED.

scope: The figure changes meaning mid-exchange. Held transcript, 12:17-12:30. Benioff first says 'we're looking at productivity levels of 30 to 50% this year in key functions like engineering, coding, support'. The interviewer restates it as 'AI is doing 30 to 50% of the work'. Benioff then adopts the restatement: 'AI is doing 30 to 50% of the work at Salesforce now'. A productivity level and a share of work done are different quantities. The circulated claim is the interviewer's framing, agreed to by the speaker. See CHANGELOG C-16.
source: Benioff (The Circuit with Emily Chang), via CNBC/Bloomberg

claim_short: 100% of the Claude Code codebase written by the model; 'no more manually written code anywhere at the company'
scope: Boris Cherny at Sequoia AI Ascent 2026. Two scopes in one talk. Narrow and dated: 'for me it's a hundred percent, the Claude Code code base', and the model 'just wrote a hundred percent of the code' from 'sometime in October or November last year' (i.e. Oct/Nov 2025). Company-wide: 'we have no more manually written code anywhere at the company, all of the SQL is written by models'. ⚠️ INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: 31 seconds earlier in the same passage he says they use Opus 4.7 to 'write most of our code'. Most and none-manual are not the same claim. See CHANGELOG C-14. ⚠️ He also says 'the model writes a hundred percent my code, I write some, usually a few dozen PRs every day', so authorship of the PR and authorship of the code are being used differently in one sentence.
source: Boris Cherny, Sequoia AI Ascent 2026 (2026-04-20), transcript held and hashed (3ec78405...8e77b614ba), 05:38-06:35 and 17:53-18:34
